anchor: Each map lands on its name (`at1`, `at2`), the claim on the claim (`head_at`), a second claim on its words (`head2_at`).

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.head: the claim, in capitals, as the voice says it ("VICE CITY ALONE: 2× LOS SANTOS"), 32 characters at most
vars.head2: a second claim that replaces the first on its words; empty = none
vars.source: who says it ("Reported by The New York Times"); empty = none
vars.map1: the smaller map: a PNG of its land with a transparent sea, cut from a real map (never a drawn one)
vars.km1: how many km the map1 image is tall: the two maps are drawn at one scale from km1 and km2
vars.sub1: under it (A) or after it in its chip (B): the place ("Los Santos")
vars.map2: the bigger map, the same way
vars.km2: how many km the map2 image is tall
vars.sub2: under its name: the place, and "fan map" when it is one ("Leonida, fan map")
vars.credit: a credit line, bottom right, for a map whose licence asks for one (CC BY); empty = none
vars.at1: seconds after the start: when map1 lands
vars.at2: seconds after the start: when map2 lands
vars.head_at: seconds after the start: when the claim lands
vars.head2_at: seconds after the start: when the second claim replaces it
vars.out: seconds after the start: when it starts to leave (the scene ends 0.3 s later)

name: Map size: laid on top
when: The voice compares the size of two game maps. The bigger real map stands in the middle; the smaller one drops onto it at the same scale with a white edge, named in a chip; the claim above with its source. Needs real map images (and the credit a fan map asks for).
